llm.summary: The AI trade got a reprieve overnight: CoreWeave raised 2026 revenue and profit guidance and popped ~15%, dragging MU, AMD, AVGO and a pre-market NVDA (+4%) with it and lifting European stocks toward records — the bubble-deflation narrative from yesterday's CPI session has been paused, not resolved. The macro backdrop got harder, not easier: Goolsbee called the inflation report 'borderline disturbing,' Yardeni is backing a 50bp December hike, Goldman has pulled forward a March hike, the dollar firmed and gold is scraping $4,040–4,050 after its CPI-driven slide. The disinflationary oil offset we leaned on yesterday has reversed — tanker attacks in the Strait of Hormuz and a drone strike on a UAE nuclear plant pushed crude to a two-week high even as Saudi output rebounds to prewar levels and OPEC added ~2mbpd in October, so supply is ample but the risk premium is back. The consumer is visibly fraying at the edges: October retail sales rose just 0.2%, the CNBC/NRF monitor shows strain beneath continued spending, and Children's Place is filing for bankruptcy. Nvidia is now two stocks in one — 10.7x forward earnings versus AVGO at 19x and AMD at 32x, against a governance discount from the Huang affair, a shareholder suit, a senator demanding his resignation and Baird cutting its target to $200 on slowing AI capex. Anthropic's bankers are pushing the IPO toward $1.5tn-plus with an Australian retail tranche, while Nscale weighs delaying its $35bn listing — the capital-absorption event of the month is real and is a claim on the same dollars currently sitting in incumbent AI megacaps. Flows still say rotation: Health Care 96, Staples 93, Real Estate 84, Materials 80 versus Technology at -77, with small caps turning positive and Value leading Growth by 111 points, though that lead is narrowing. Bonds are closed for Veterans Day, so today's tape is thin and offers no yield confirmation — discount the moves.

market_thesis.short_term: Index neutral with violent internal rotation and a thin, bond-closed tape. CoreWeave's guidance raise buys the AI complex a relief rally that is tactically real — contracted neocloud revenue is a cash-flow fact — but it does not change the discount rate, and a December hike (possibly 50bp) is now the working assumption. Expect continued dispersion: cash-generative value, insurers, healthcare distribution, staples and energy infrastructure bid; long-duration narrative AI (PLTR -19%), crypto, housing-linked and gold-levered positions pressured. Oil's bounce on Hormuz removes yesterday's margin tailwind for DAL and FDX; watch whether it sticks or fades as OPEC supply reasserts. The Anthropic book-build into its listing is the dominant liquidity variable of the next two weeks.
market_thesis.medium_term: Reflation (33.7, +10.5) and Stagflation (33.2, +12.5) are tied with Goldilocks gutted at 16.7 — a tightening central bank into an economy that is not breaking. That means higher-for-longer nominal yields, a firm dollar, compressed multiples on duration, and persistent capital rotation into Health Care, Staples, Real Estate, Materials and Financials. Inside AI the split sharpens from 'chips versus everything' to 'contracted electrons, hardware and permits versus storytelling and credit': gas-plant construction costs +66%, uranium expansion plans in Uzbekistan and Europe, midstream firms expanding gas pipelines on data-center demand. Two mega-listings (Anthropic ~$1.5tn, SpaceX) will force passive reconstitution and drain incremental capital from incumbent AI holdings — the underrated risk to the existing megacap complex. A slowing consumer (retail sales +0.2%) into a hiking Fed is the classic setup for consumer bifurcation: value retail and essentials gain share, mid-market discretionary breaks.
market_thesis.long_term: Energy, permits and political consent are the binding constraints on AI, and the economics accrue to whoever owns generation, grid hardware, copper, gas and nuclear fuel rather than to whoever owns the narrative. AI leadership has become a national-security variable — the Nvidia spying case, export-control pressure and Bessent's 'harbor no illusions' framing on China — which permanently raises the risk premium on China-exposed semis and embeds duplicated, higher-cost supply chains and a higher inflation floor. Reshoring attention (+58% versus 28-day base) and chip-fab search interest say the industrial capex cycle has public mindshare, not just institutional. Market structure itself is changing: 24-hour US trading, crypto venues attacking equity order flow, and the world's largest private companies listing in New York concentrate global capital and index risk in US listings. For households, affordability — electricity, groceries, insurance premiums, housing, retirement — is the dominant structural variable, entrenching value retail, generics and distribution, insurance and experiences over undifferentiated discretionary.

short_term: Consumers are still spending but trading down: October retail sales +0.2% is the slowest pace in months, the CNBC/NRF monitor flags strain, and Children's Place is filing for bankruptcy — money anxiety is now expressed as channel shift, not abstinence.

Investors are reflexively dip-buying AI on any good datapoint (CRWV) while simultaneously pulling capital out of the sector in aggregate (Technology flows -77) — a behavioural split between tactical traders and allocators.

Households are seeking yield and safety as rate-hike bets build: long-duration Treasury flows increasing, dividend-income content proliferating, and gold holding on central-bank demand rather than retail demand.

Public attention is migrating from AI as abstraction to AI as physical neighbour — 'ai data center near me', 'ai data center water usage' — the first sign of local political friction over siting and resources.

Retail investors are being invited into the AI capital stack directly (Anthropic's Australian retail tranche), a classic late-stage democratisation of access that shifts risk from institutions to households.

Corporates are hedging guidance: NOV cut on Iran war costs, Applied Aerospace lowered revenue guidance, Appear withdrew guidance entirely — management teams are buying optionality on an uncertain cost base.
long_term: Energy is becoming a consumer-visible household cost and a political object; electricity price inflation driven by data-center load will shape voting, siting and utility regulation for a decade.

Security — of data, of borders, of supply chains — is displacing convenience as the marginal thing people and firms will pay for: cybersecurity leads flows, 'data breach' queries are rising, and defence orders are lifting guidance.

Health and healthspan spending is structurally inelastic and increasingly where discretionary dollars go; Health Care at 96 on flows is not a trade, it is where capital goes when households prioritise bodies over objects.
Knowledge and productivity are being bought as software subscriptions rather than headcount, which depresses white-collar hiring and raises the political salience of AI displacement.

Housing illiquidity under higher-for-longer rates pushes demand into renovation, repair and smaller-footprint living rather than transactions — supporting the materials and improvement complex over homebuilders.
Mobility and travel remain status-and-experience purchases people defend late into a slowdown, but they are highly levered to fuel prices, which are now re-exposed to Hormuz geopolitics.
